about: The Pocketknife catalogue (docs/pt/WORKSHOP-V2-SPEC.md, section 5.4). node tools/gen.mjs generates tools/<id>/spec.md, tools/<id>/tool.test.js and TASKS.md from it. Format in tools/CONTRACT.md.

tools.title: Word count and reading time
tools.concept: Counts the words and characters of a text and estimates how many minutes it takes to read.
rules: A word is a run of letters (with or without accents) and digits. A hyphen (-) or an apostrophe (' or ’) between two letters or digits does not split it: "well-known" and "isn’t" are 1 word each. Punctuation on its own ("—", "...") is not a word.
Numbers count as words: "In 2024 I read 12 books." has 6 words.
characters counts every character that is not a space, a tab or a line break (punctuation counts).
reading_minutes = words ÷ words per minute, rounded up to whole minutes (Math.ceil): 1 word gives 1 minute and a text with no words gives 0.
With no words per minute filled in, use 200.

in.text: The well-known café — again, isn't it?

First line.

  Second   line, it’s here.

errors.error: Words per minute: the minimum is 1.

tools.title: Title case
tools.concept: Capitalises a title the way books and films do, however it was typed.
rules: Each word starts with a capital letter and the rest of the word is lower case.
Extra spaces (at the start, at the end and between words) become a single space.

spec_gaps.what: what to do with small words such as of, the, and or in
spec_gaps.rule: Small words (a, an, the, and, but, or, nor, for, of, in, on, at, to, by) stay lower case, except when they are the first word of the title: "the lord of the rings" gives "The Lord of the Rings".

tools.title: URL slug
tools.concept: Turns a title into a slug for a web address: lower case, no accents and with hyphens.
rules: Removes the accents: decompose the text (normalize('NFD')) and remove the diacritical marks (U+0300 to U+036F). "Café" becomes "Cafe".
Turns everything into lower case.
Each run of characters that are not a-z or 0-9 becomes a single hyphen: spaces, punctuation, _, &, $, and also letters that do not decompose, such as ß or ø.
Removes the hyphens at the start and at the end.
If no letter or digit is left, returns the error in the table.

errors.error: The text has no letters or digits for the slug.

tools.title: Remove accents
tools.concept: Removes the accents from a text and leaves everything else as it is.
rules: Removes the diacritical marks from letters: á, à, â, ã → a; é, è, ê → e; ç → c; ñ → n; ü → u; and the same in capitals (É → E, Ç → C). One way: normalize('NFD'), remove the characters U+0300 to U+036F and normalize('NFC').
Letters that are not a base letter with an accent, such as ß, ø, æ or œ, stay the same.
Everything else stays exactly as it is: upper and lower case, spaces (also at the start and at the end), line breaks, punctuation and digits.

tools.title: Count the occurrences of a word
tools.concept: Counts how many times a word appears in a text, only as a whole word.
rules: The words of the text are the runs of letters (with or without accents) and digits. Everything else separates words, including spaces, punctuation, hyphens and apostrophes: "rain-coat" has the words "rain" and "coat", and "it's" has "it" and "s".
Only whole words count: "sea" does not count in "seal" or "overseas".
Upper and lower case do not matter ("Sea", "SEA" and "sea" are the same), but accents do: "café" and "cafe" are different words.
The word searched for (without the spaces at the start and at the end) must be a single word, with only letters and digits; if it is not, returns the error in the table.

in.text: The sea, the SEA and the Sea.
A seal by the sea, overseas

errors.error: Type a single word, with no spaces or punctuation.

tools.title: X % of Y and Y is what % of X
tools.concept: The two everyday percentage sums: how much a percentage of a value is, and what percentage one value is of another.
rules: x_percent_of_y = X × Y / 100.
y_percent_of_x = Y / X × 100.
Both results are rounded to 2 decimal places (Math.round(v × 100) / 100 is fine).

tools.title: Rule of three
tools.concept: If A matches B, what does C match? The rule of three for direct proportions.
rules: X = B × C ÷ A (direct proportion: A is to B as C is to X).
Round X to 2 decimal places (Math.round(v × 100) / 100 is fine).
A, B and C may be negative or have decimal places; only A cannot be 0.

tools.title: Round to decimal places
tools.concept: Rounds a number to the number of decimal places you choose.
rules: Rounds the number to `places` decimal places and returns a number.
With no places filled in, use 2.

errors.error: Decimal places: type a whole number.

spec_gaps.what: how to round the cases that sit exactly halfway, such as 1.005 to 2 places
spec_gaps.rule: Cases exactly halfway, in decimal, round up: 1.005 to 2 places gives 1.01 and 2.675 to 2 places gives 2.68. Mind floating point: in JavaScript 1.005 * 100 is 100.49999…, so Math.round(v * 100) / 100 and toFixed(2) both give 1.

tools.title: Mean and median of a list
tools.concept: Works out the mean and the median of a list of numbers.
rules: The numbers are separated by commas, semicolons, spaces or line breaks. The point is the decimal mark ("1.5" is one and a half). There is no thousands separator.
Each number may have a sign (-5, +3). An item that is not a number gives the error "<item>" is not a number., with the item as it was typed (the first one that fails).
count is how many numbers there are.
mean is the sum ÷ count. median is the middle number once they are sorted from smallest to largest; with an even count, it is the mean of the two middle ones.
mean and median are rounded to 2 decimal places (Math.round(v × 100) / 100 is fine).

tools.title: Roman ↔ Arabic numerals
tools.concept: Converts Arabic numbers (1, 2, 3…) into Roman numerals (I, II, III…) and back.
rules: direction to_roman: value must have only digits and be a whole number from 1 to 3999 (no sign and no decimal places); if it is not, returns the error in the table.

Roman numerals are written in the standard form, in capitals, from the largest value to the smallest: M = 1000, CM = 900, D = 500, CD = 400, C = 100, XC = 90, L = 50, XL = 40, X = 10, IX = 9, V = 5, IV = 4, I = 1 (4 is IV, never IIII).
direction to_arabic: accepts upper or lower case ("xiv" = "XIV") and returns the number as text ("14").

Only a numeral in the standard form is valid, the one to_roman would write for that number (1 to 3999). "IIII", "IC", "VX", "MMMM" or letters other than I, V, X, L, C, D, M give the error "<value>" is not a valid Roman numeral., with value as it was typed.
The output is always a text.

errors.error: For Roman numerals, type a whole number from 1 to 3999.
"IIII" is not a valid Roman numeral.

tools.title: Days between two dates
tools.concept: How many days there are from one date to another.
rules: Returns end − start in days: from 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-02 is 1, and the same date gives 0.
If end is before start, the result is negative.
Leap years count (February 2024 has 29 days). These are calendar dates, with no times or time zones: working in UTC (Date.UTC) avoids daylight saving time errors.

errors.error: Start date: type a date as YYYY-MM-DD.
End date: type a date as YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.title: Age on a date
tools.concept: How many full years old a person is on a date of your choice.
rules: Returns the full years from birth to on. Each year is complete on the birthday: the day itself already counts.
Someone born on 29 February has their birthday on 29 February in leap years and on 28 February in the other years.
Leap years: those divisible by 4, except those divisible by 100 that are not divisible by 400 (2000 is one, 1900 is not).
on equal to birth gives 0. on before birth gives the error in the table.

errors.error: The date must be on or after the date of birth.
Date of birth: type a date as YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.title: Day of the week of a date
tools.concept: Tells which day of the week a date falls (or fell) on.
rules: Returns the English name of the day, with a capital letter: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday or Sunday.
Uses the Gregorian calendar, also for dates before 1582. Works in UTC (getUTCDay), so that it does not depend on the computer's time zone.

errors.error: Date: type a date as YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.title: Add days to a date
tools.concept: Which date it is N days from now, or was N days ago.
rules: Adds days to the date (a negative number subtracts) and returns the date as YYYY-MM-DD, with leading zeros (2024-02-01).
Respects the length of each month and leap years: 2024-02-28 + 1 gives 2024-02-29 and 2023-02-28 + 1 gives 2023-03-01.
Works in UTC, so that daylight saving time does not change the day.
If the result falls outside the calendar (before 0001-01-01 or after 9999-12-31), returns the error in the table.

errors.error: The result falls outside the calendar (0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31).

tools.title: Time in another zone (fixed offset)
tools.concept: Converts a time from one zone to another, given their offsets from UTC (no daylight saving time), and says whether the day changes.
rules: time is a 24-hour HH:MM time from 00:00 to 23:59: the hour may have 1 or 2 digits (9:30 is 09:30) and the minutes have 2. Anything else gives the error in the table for Time.

zone_a and zone_b are offsets from UTC as +HH:MM or -HH:MM (the sign is required, 2 digits on each side), with minutes 00, 15, 30 or 45, from -12:00 to +14:00. Anything else gives the error in the table, starting with the name of the zone (Zone A or Zone B).
The inputs are checked in this order: Time, Zone A, Zone B (the first error is the one returned).
direction a_to_b: the time is in zone A and the result is the time in zone B. direction b_to_a: the time is in zone B and the result is the time in zone A.
The sum: target time = source time − source offset + target offset. The returned time is always HH:MM, with 2 digits in each part.

day says which day the target time falls on compared with the day of the source time: "same day", "next day", "previous day", "2 days later" or "2 days earlier" (the last two only happen between zones far apart, such as -12:00 and +14:00).

errors.error: Time: type a time as HH:MM, from 00:00 to 23:59.
Zone A: type an offset as +HH:MM or -HH:MM, from -12:00 to +14:00.
Zone B: type an offset as +HH:MM or -HH:MM, from -12:00 to +14:00.

tools.title: Tip and split the bill
tools.concept: At a group dinner: how much the tip is and how much each person pays.
rules: Tip = total × percentage / 100, rounded to the cent.
Total with tip = total + tip.
Each person pays the total with tip divided by the number of people, with 2 decimal places.

spec_gaps.what: how to round each person's share
spec_gaps.rule: Each person's share rounds up to the cent, so the shares never add up to less than the total: 100 with no tip for 3 people gives 33.34 each (33.33 × 3 = 99.99 is not enough). An exact split stays the same (60 for 3 gives 20).

tools.title: Generate a UUID v4
tools.concept: Generates random unique identifiers in the UUID version 4 format, for tests and sample data.
rules: Returns a list of `count` v4 UUIDs, in lower case: 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal digits.
In the third group the first digit is 4 (the version); in the fourth group the first digit is 8, 9, a or b (the variant).
Use the random() that run receives (never Math.random), so that the same seed gives the same result.
